title: Legatics joins Legora’s integration ecosystem, giving Legora read and write access to live deals
summary: Legora is the collaborative AI powering lawyers to review and research faster, draft smarter, and advise with precision. Legora adapts to your ways of working, unlocking team and machine collaboration at scale.
body_markdown:
Lawyers using Legora can now ask questions of their live transactions in Legatics and create or update checklists, trackers and issues lists from the work they do in Legora, with each firm’s permissions applied.


[Legatics](https://www.legatics.com/) , the transaction management platform used by leading law firms around the world, today announced that it has joined Legora’s[product integration ecosystem](https://legora.com/product/integrations) . The integration connects Legatics to[Legora](https://legora.com/) , so lawyers working in Legora can see the current state of their deals in Legatics and make changes to them without switching between the two.


Legora is the agentic operating system for legal work. Many of those lawyers are using it for review and drafting on the same complex transactions they are running in Legatics. The information about those transactions, such as what is outstanding, who is responsible for it, what has been signed and what has changed, sits in Legatics. Connecting the two means the Legora Agent can work from that information directly and put the results of its work back onto the deal, where the rest of the deal team, the client and the other side can see it and act on it.


#### **What the integration does**


**Ask questions of the live deal.** Legora can read matter data held in Legatics, including the status of checklists and trackers, who is responsible for each item, parties, deadlines, comments left by the deal team, and the contents of data rooms and closing binders. A lawyer can ask where a single deal stands or which of their matters need attention this week, and the answer comes from Legatics as it is at that moment. This makes routine reporting much quicker. An associate asked by a partner or client for a status update can have Legora pull the open items, owners and latest comments from Legatics and draft the update in minutes.


**Update live deals in Legatics, directly from Legora.** Legora can also create and update content in Legatics. For example, a lawyer can do the following directly on Legora:


-


review a facility agreement in Legora and create a conditions precedent checklist in Legatics from the Conditions Precedent schedule


-


update the status of checklist items in Legatics as documents are reviewed in Legora


-


record follow-ups from a document review in Legora on a Legatics list, with owners and deadlines


-


build a closing checklist, issues list or documents list in a Legatics matter, with the right columns and starter rows


Once that content is in Legatics, it is tracked like everything else on the deal, so the next time someone asks where things stand, the answer is updated to reflect work done in Legora.


Legora can only see or change what the individual user can already see or change in Legatics. Write access is optional and is switched on by the firm. Every change made through the integration is recorded in the matter’s audit trail, and administrators can turn the connection off at any time. The integration is available to all mutual customers at no additional cost.


“Lawyers want their AI tools to work from the deal as it actually stands, and then do something useful with what they find. Being able to read from Legatics is helpful, but being able to write back to it is what moves a transaction forward. Legora Agent can now do both, under the same permissions firms already rely on for everyone working on the matter,” said Anthony Seale, Founder and CEO of Legatics.


“This came directly from our mutual customers. Their lawyers are doing more and more of their analysis and drafting in Legora, but the deal itself is run in Legatics, and copying work from one to the other by hand costs time and means things get missed. We think of Legatics as the infrastructure transactions run on, whether the work is done by a person or an agent, and connecting it to Legora with read and write from the start is an important part of that,” said Rob MacAdam, Chief Product & Strategy Officer at Legatics.


“AI is most useful on a transaction when it knows where the deal really stands. Legatics is where our deal teams keep track of that, connecting it to Legora means our lawyers get answers that reflect the live position on each matter, and can keep Legatics up to date as the deal moves, all without leaving Legora,” said Isabel Parker, Chief Innovation Officer at White & Case.


“Legatics is where many of our customers keep track of their deals, and Legora is where the legal work is done. This integration ensures the legal work on Legora is grounded in the latest status of the deal. A lawyer can now bring in the deal status as context when updating documents in Legora, and then use Legora to directly reflect any further changes or action items in Legatics,” said Gabriel Quek, Senior Director of Technology Partnerships at Legora.


#### **About Legatics**


Legatics is a transaction management platform that helps lawyers collaborate on and close complex deals. Designed by lawyers, it replaces the checklists, emails and spreadsheets traditionally used to run transactions with a single collaborative platform covering conditions precedent, closing checklists, signing, data rooms and closing binders. Legatics is used by leading law firms around the world.


#### **About Legora**


Legora is the agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review, and drafting across complex matters. It is used by more than 140,000 legal professionals at more than 2,500 leading law firms and in-house legal teams across over 80 markets.
